title: Feeding Our Future — warning, authority, response, and later findings
purpose: Separate warnings received, oversight actions, court activity, law-enforcement referrals, later criminal allegations, and audit findings without inferring criminal intent by public officials.

events.summary: OLA says MDE received the first of at least 30 complaints involving Feeding Our Future or its sites beginning in June 2018; complaints continued through December 2021.
events.source_locator: report p.49; PDF index 56
events.qualification: Complaint received does not mean complaint substantiated.

events.summary: OLA says recruitment-related complaints began in July 2018 and later found MDE repeatedly assigned initial fact-finding/dispute resolution to Feeding Our Future and the complainant.
events.source_locator: report p.55; PDF index 62

events.summary: MDE conducted its only CACFP administrative review of Feeding Our Future. OLA says it resulted in 22 findings across 11 of 13 review areas and required follow-up, but MDE never conducted a follow-up review.
events.source_locator: report pp.37, 40-41; PDF text pp.44, 47-48

events.summary: MDE began an SFSP administrative review after Feeding Our Future entered SFSP; OLA says the review was paused in October 2020 after virtual site visits were not working and was not completed.
events.source_locator: report pp.41-42; PDF text pp.48-49
events.qualification: OLA acknowledged COVID-19 and waiver conditions affected decisions but said MDE could have used other review methods.

events.summary: OLA's timeline records a sponsor complaint alleging fraud in CACFP and SFSP, including an alleged fraud ring.
events.source_locator: Appendix A; PDF p.92 text extraction
events.qualification: The complaint itself was an allegation, not an adjudicated finding.

events.summary: MDE officials told OLA that MDE escalated concerns about Feeding Our Future to USDA OIG in October or November 2020, primarily concerning the sponsor's growth. OLA says the exact date was unclear.
events.source_locator: report p.50 / Appendix A; PDF p.57 and p.92 text extraction
events.qualification: The corpus still lacks USDA OIG's own Minnesota-specific work product showing what it did with the referral.

events.summary: Per HuffPost's reporting on the 2024 OLA audit, MDE alerted USDA that Feeding Our Future's reimbursements had risen approximately 252% while statewide reimbursements rose about 14% over the same period, and separately flagged 'perfect daycare attendance over an extended period' at FOF sites as a fraud indicator.
events.qualification: Sourced to a news article's characterization of the OLA audit; the exact 252%/14% figures were not independently located in this corpus's own copy of the OLA report text.

events.summary: HuffPost reports, citing the 2024 OLA audit, that 'USDA was unresponsive' and 'pushed responsibility back to MDE,' and that USDA told MDE the perfect-attendance pattern 'would be possible due to the waivers' in effect during the pandemic.
events.qualification: An anonymous former USDA official is separately quoted by HuffPost describing internal recognition that the numbers looked like fraud and a decision by superiors not to get involved; that quote is anonymous-sourced and not independently corroborated by a named official or a USDA/USDA-OIG document.

events.summary: Feeding Our Future sued MDE over handling of applications for new food-distribution sites and race-discrimination claims.
events.source_locator: Judicial Branch lines 23-26

events.summary: The parties reached an agreement and the court approved a consent order requiring MDE to handle federally regulated site applications reasonably promptly.
events.source_locator: Judicial Branch lines 25-26
events.qualification: This order concerned application processing; it was not an order to resume reimbursement payments.

events.summary: MDE issued a first set of serious deficiencies for CACFP and SFSP tied to nonprofit-status and federal audit-requirement issues.
events.source_locator: Chapter 5 timeline, report p.63; PDF index 70

events.summary: OLA says the FBI notified MDE in February 2021 of allegations it had received involving Feeding Our Future; OLA notes those allegations would later be reflected in federal charges.
events.source_locator: report p.65; PDF p.72 text extraction

events.summary: MDE initiated a process to terminate Feeding Our Future's CACFP sponsorship after determining the January serious deficiencies were not fully corrected.
events.source_locator: Appendix A report p.88; PDF index 95

events.summary: MDE issued a second set of serious deficiencies related to financial viability/management, administrative capabilities, and program accountability. OLA records that MDE also stopped paying Feeding Our Future reimbursement claims and stopped issuing site IDs for new sites.
events.source_locator: Appendix A report p.88; PDF index 95

events.summary: According to MDE as recorded by OLA, USDA Midwest Regional Office supported MDE's decision to stop reimbursement payments and indicated MDE had authority to do so.
events.source_locator: Appendix A report p.88; PDF index 95
events.qualification: This is OLA's record of what MDE said USDA told it; a USDA record would be stronger for the federal position.

events.summary: OLA records that MDE provided the FBI information about fraud suspicions involving Feeding Our Future and sponsored sites; MDE believed some sites were submitting fraudulent documents and inflating meal counts. OLA says the FBI began an investigation in May 2021.
events.source_locator: Appendix A report p.88; PDF index 95

events.summary: Feeding Our Future moved for a temporary restraining order challenging MDE's withholding of reimbursements and separately sought to hold MDE in contempt over application processing under the December 2020 consent order.
events.source_locator: OLA Appendix A, report p.89 / PDF p.96; Judicial Branch lines 28-29
events.qualification: The application-processing contempt issue and the reimbursement stop-pay issue were legally distinct.

events.summary: At the hearing, the court determined MDE's stop-pay issue was outside the scope of the existing lawsuit and therefore not within its jurisdiction in that case, while also characterizing MDE's nonpayment as a serious problem. No order requiring payment resumption issued.
events.source_locator: OLA report p.69 / Appendix A p.89; Judicial Branch lines 28-35; Korte transcript pp.130-132
events.qualification: The court's comments influenced MDE's later decision according to OLA and Korte, but comments are not an order.

events.summary: Feeding Our Future filed a Motion-Contempt (Index #32, 11 pages) two days after the April 21 hearing, one week before MDE removed the stop-pay.
events.source_locator: Register of Actions, 04/23/2021 Index #32
events.qualification: The motion text itself was not retrieved (docket index/metadata only); its specific legal basis and requested relief are not yet confirmed.

events.summary: A second Temporary Restraining Order Hearing was held before Judge Guthmann at 3:00 PM (remote), the same calendar day MDE voluntarily removed the stop-pay per OLA's timeline. The docket records several same-day filings (two 25-page 'Other Document' entries, two attorney affidavits, a 5-page brief, and a 3-page affidavit) and an 'Order for Submissions-Under Advisement' issued that day.
events.source_locator: Register of Actions, 04/30/2021 hearing record and Index #42-#50
events.qualification: This second hearing was not previously reflected in this corpus's timeline, which had described only the April 21 hearing as preceding the April 30 resumption. The docket establishes the hearing and MDE's decision were contemporaneous; it does not establish which caused which, and neither OLA's account nor Korte's 2026 interview specifically references this second hearing. Treat as an open sequencing question, not a resolved causal link.

events.summary: MDE removed Feeding Our Future's stop-pay in its claims system and voluntarily resumed reimbursements. OLA says MDE removed the stop-pay because of the court's April 21 statements; the Judicial Branch confirms no court order required resumption. In a 2026 transcribed interview, Daron Korte recalled that MDE internally chose to lift the stop-pay rather than force a likely adverse ruling and additional sanctions.
events.source_locator: OLA Appendix A p.89 / PDF p.96; Judicial Branch lines 28-35; Korte transcript pp.130-132
events.qualification: Korte identified himself, Monica Herrera, and Emily Honer as participants in the internal discussion; recalled Heather Mueller was informed rather than asked for approval; said MDE's AG litigating attorneys were involved; and said he did not think the Governor's Office made the decision, though its education policy and legal advisers would have been updated. Those participant/rationale details are retrospective recollection, not a contemporaneous decision memo. The Ramsey County docket additionally shows this decision fell on the same day as a second, previously-uncaptured TRO hearing (see the preceding event); Korte's account does not specifically address that hearing.

events.summary: MDE vacated the proposed termination/disqualification notice and deferred the first set of serious deficiencies.
events.source_locator: Chapter 5 timeline, report p.63; PDF index 70

events.summary: MDE deferred the second set of serious deficiencies. OLA says Feeding Our Future was then no longer under any serious deficiencies and could continue operating; OLA later found MDE lacked sufficient evidence that the deficiencies had been fully and permanently addressed.
events.source_locator: report pp.63-65; PDF pp.70-72

events.summary: The Minnesota Judicial Branch says the law-enforcement investigation became public in January 2022.
events.source_locator: Judicial Branch line 24

events.summary: DOJ announced charges against 47 defendants in the initial public charging wave, alleging a roughly $250 million scheme involving Federal Child Nutrition Program funds.
events.qualification: Charging allegations are not adjudicated findings, and the $250 million figure is not a restitution/collection total.

events.actor: Minnesota Judicial Branch / Ramsey County District Court
events.summary: The Judicial Branch issued a correction stating Judge Guthmann never ordered MDE to resume food reimbursement payments and that all such resumed payments were made voluntarily by MDE.
events.source_locator: Judicial Branch lines 20-35

events.actor: Minnesota Office of the Legislative Auditor
events.summary: OLA concluded MDE's inadequate oversight created opportunities for fraud, citing warning signs, application/administrative-review failures, complaint-investigation failures, and shortcomings in the serious-deficiency process.
events.qualification: OLA did not find that MDE officials joined the criminal fraud scheme.

events.actor: U.S. House Committee on Education and the Workforce
events.recipient: Gov. Tim Walz; Minnesota Department of Education; USDA Secretary Tom Vilsack; USDA Inspector General Phyllis Fong
events.summary: Committee Chairwoman Virginia Foxx issued subpoenas to Walz, MDE, USDA, and USDA's Inspector General compelling production of records on oversight of Feeding Our Future, stating MDE's prior production had been 'neither timely nor fully responsive.' Documents were due by noon on 2024-09-18.
events.qualification: Issued by the committee's Republican majority; underlying allegations against Walz/MDE/USDA are committee characterizations, not adjudicated findings. No public record of USDA or USDA OIG's compliance, production, or response to this subpoena was located in this research pass.

derived_conclusions.conclusion: The record supports a long warning-and-oversight-failure chronology beginning before the pandemic, while also showing MDE took some significant enforcement/referral actions in 2020-2021.

The primary record contradicts the claim that Judge Guthmann forced MDE to resume Feeding Our Future reimbursements. OLA fixes the voluntary resumption date at April 30, 2021, and Korte's later participant account supplies an internal rationale without converting the judge's comments into an order.

The internal payment-resumption chain is now substantially identified through Korte's participant account, but contemporaneous MDE deliberation records and the substance of privileged Attorney General legal advice remain unverified.

The current primary/audit record supports oversight and administrative-failure propositions but does not, without actor-specific evidence, establish that a named MDE or statewide elected official knowingly joined the fraudulent scheme.
